title: Kansas City musicians from his autobiography notes
summary: Reading from his notes, he lists Kansas City figures including Eddie Durham, Jesse Stone and Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You know, when I told you that I went to, you know... from Oklahoma City to Kansas City, and then I said that Kansas City had become the jazz capital overnight, and I also said it was very common to see Louis Armstrong, Count Basie, Vic Dickenson, Lester Young, Walter Page, Lips Page, Jack Washington, Jimmy Rushing, Big Joe Turner, Julia Lee, Bennie Moten, Eddie Durham, who was a factor, and a tremendous factor in the total structure of those territorial bands, because he was a prolific writer and, you know what I mean, was a great guy.

I first saw Eddie in 1925 with his brothers. They had The Durham Brothers' Band. They came from Terrell, Texas and I first saw them around the same time Alphonso Trent showed up around Dallas. And I said Jesse Stone, Pete Johnson, Walter Page and Hot Lips Page. Emil Williams was a very, very

famous piano player. I called his name to you. And Buddy Tate. Buddy and I started playing the same day. Budd Johnson, Bennie Moten and his brother, Buster. Willie Mack Washington. Willie Mack Washington I knew in Waco, Texas in 1914. Joe Turner. Alvin Burroughs' was a drummer that I think was with Earl Hines.
Right, and Mary Lou...Ben Thigpen, and a lot of visiting musicians. But I just happened to see this, and then I thought about, you know what I mean, just reviewing some of these names.
